A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sable research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results across 45 tasks, agent-scaling experiments on LBF and Neom, and architectural and memory ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark, scaling and ablation results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the stated critic update from adding the squared-error gradient to subtracting it. The architecture, PPO objective, episode resets and scaling procedures otherwise remain. This establishes a correction to the printed algorithm, not that the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 45 tasks across RWARE, LBF, Connector, SMAX, MABrax and MPE, plus the same LBF and Neom scaling scenarios. The added illustrative grid world and Neom diagrams do not establish additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: MAT, MAPPO, IPPO, QMIX, MASAC and HASAC retain the same task-specific participation. The scaling comparators and modified-MAT ablation variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated training budgets, evaluation intervals, episode counts, tuning procedure and hyperparameter settings are unchanged. However, the SMAX per-task curves change substantially in scale while retaining the same metric label. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects a metric or normalization change, or a reporting correction.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same RMSNorm/SwiGLU, memory-removal and chunk-size ablations. The agent-scaling experiments and positional-encoding findings are also retained. The new environment illustrations explain existing setups rather than add supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 independent trials, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, stratified bootstrap intervals for environment aggregates, and the same probability-of-improvement significance criterion.

E6.justification: The SMAX curves in v4 Figure 12 are replaced in v5 Figure 13: for example, the 2s3z plateau changes from approximately 2 to approximately 1 under the unchanged 'Mean episode return' label. Tables 1–6, the other result plots and the 34-of-45 headline finding remain unchanged. The unexplained plotted changes cannot be interpreted as same-setting performance losses.

T1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the formal problem specification, introducing latent states, state-based transitions and rewards, and set-valued observation distributions instead of the earlier observation-based formulation and independent policy factorization. New Appendix A formalizes observation support for IL, CTDE and centralized learning. Equation 6 also changes the chunkwise mathematical specification, including its decay exponent and the hidden state used in the output; these changes exceed equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The scientific headline claims—RetNet-based policy learning, superiority on 34 of 45 tasks and thousand-agent scaling—remain. The data/code contribution changes from a promised release of data and reproduction scripts to an asserted completed public release, also emphasized in the abstract.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly characterizes Sable as centralized. New Appendix A explains why pooled observations can remain partially observable and acknowledges that centralized execution receives more information than IL/CTDE, at additional inference cost. Section 3 also ties the retained convergence claim more explicitly to PPO and heterogeneous-agent mirror learning.

D1.justification: v4 provides a Mava implementation but postpones experimental data, task hyperparameters and reproduction instructions. v5 supplies a project-site access point and reports availability of those resources plus frozen experimental code, distinguished from maintained Mava code. Appendix E.2.4 additionally documents categorical and Gaussian action heads, including the shared log-standard-deviation parameter.

R1.justification: v5 adds Dec-POMDP references, including Kaelbling et al. and Oliehoek et al., and software references in expanded acknowledgements. Its central positioning relative to MAT, RetNet and prior MARL approaches remains; the changed Liu citation suffixes identify the same existing works.

P1.justification: v5 copyedits the prose, expands selected background and training explanations, moves Algorithm 1 into the main text, and reorganizes appendix headings around a new Background appendix. It also expands acknowledgements and adds an impact statement. Most existing paragraphs and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references adopt a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures, tables and pseudocode. Figure 1 moves to the first page, the MARL-spectrum triangle is removed, and two Neom illustrations are added. The appendix task plots are enlarged and their SMAX panels redrawn.

improvement.justification: The reported frozen-code/data release, added implementation details and corrected critic-update sign improve reproducibility. However, v5 Equation 6 uses updated h_i in the retention output where v4 used incoming memory, creating an inconsistency with the retained incoming-state explanation. Its SMAX curves also change without explaining the metric while the tables stay fixed. These documentation gains coexist with material mathematical and reporting ambiguities, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
